blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Deployment keeps identical Pods running. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: This one also keeps its Pods away from each other.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to watch where its Pods land.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web

blocks.title: Three copies and their label
blocks.what: Keep three Pods running, and manage the Pods labelled app: spread-web.
blocks.why: If all three ran on one node, losing that node would stop the app.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Three copies of the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread-web

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. It gives each Pod the selector’s label.
blocks.why: The rule in the next block looks for this same label.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread-web

blocks.title: Keep away from these Pods
blocks.what: podAntiAffinity keeps a Pod away from other Pods that match labelSelector.
blocks.why: required… makes it a hard rule. A Pod waits rather than break it.
blocks.ifRemoved: The scheduler may put several copies on the same node.
blocks.comment: Hard rule: do not place this Pod near Pods with these labels
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - labelSelector:
                matchLabels:

blocks.title: Apart by node
blocks.what: The rule matches the Deployment’s own label. topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname means “near” is the same node.
blocks.why: So no two spread-web Pods share a node. A zone label would spread them across zones instead.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because the rule needs a topologyKey.
blocks.comment: No two of these Pods on the same node
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - labelSelector:
                matchLabels:
                  app: spread-web
              topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: Each Pod runs one nginx container. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: With three nodes, each node gets exactly one Pod.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread-web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread-web
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - labelSelector:
                matchLabels:
                  app: spread-web
              topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.30.4

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is spread-web.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: spread-web, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: The nginx web server, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.affinity: Rules that attract Pods to nodes, or keep them near or apart from other Pods.
notes.spec.template.spec.affinity.podAntiAffin: Rules that keep this Pod away from other Pods.
Hard rules: a Pod waits in Pending rather than break them.
Which Pods to keep away from.
Pods with all of these labels count.
Keep away from Pods labelled app: spread-web, the other copies of this app.
A node label that defines “near”. kubernetes.io/hostname is unique per node, so near means the same node.

tryIt.result: Three Running Pods. The NODE column shows a different node for each.

check.run: kubectl get pods -l app=spread-web --field-selector status.phase=Running -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u

tryIt.result: Removes the Deployment and its Pods.

questions.question: Which Pods does each spread-web Pod keep away from?
questions.explain: The labelSelector picks the Pods to avoid. Here that is the other copies of the same app.

questions.question: What does topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname mean here?
answers: Two copies may not share a node
Two copies may not share a zone
questions.explain: Every node has its own hostname label. Nodes with the same value count as the same place.

questions.question: How would preferredDuringScheduling… change the rule?
answers: Kubernetes would try to spread the Pods, but place them anyway if it cannot
It would spread Pods across zones
questions.explain: A preferred rule is a wish, not a must. The class file uses it so extra copies still run.

fix.expect: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 node\(s\) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules
fix.message: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules.
fix.explain: Four copies cannot each have their own node when the cluster has three. The fourth Pod waits in Pending.
fix.fix: Ask for no more copies than nodes, here 3, or make the rule preferred.
